shippingNews.postTitle: Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Seaway Tonnage Up 3.5 Percent Through End of September

stories.body: Saltwater tanker transits the St. Lawrence Seaway. [Photo SLSMC] WELLAND CANAL – Nearly 25 million tonnes of cargo passed through the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Seaway System by the end of September, up 3.5 per cent compared to the same time last year. It’s the second positive increase of the 2026 season, which began with March openings of the Welland Canal and Montreal-Lake Ontario sections of the 3,700-kilometre-long waterway. shippingNews.postTitle: Manistee Harbor Tours to Close Season with Fall Color Tours

stories.body: MANISTEE, MI – Manistee Harbor Tours will wrap up its 2026 sailing season with special fall color cruises aboard the Princess of Manistee this weekend and next weekend, offering passengers an opportunity to view the autumn scenery along Lake Michigan and the Manistee River. The two-hour cruises are scheduled from 2 to 4 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, Oct. 24-25, and again Oct. 31 and Nov. 1. These will be the final scheduled cruises of the year for the 65-foot passenger vessel. Capt. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: 30.5 inch high pressure extending from southern Quebec into New England is extending a 30.2 inch ridge over Lake Superior. By Saturday afternoon, a 29.2 inch low over northern Manitoba drags a 30.1 inch trough over the west half of Lake Superior. The trough remains over the lake until Saturday night. High pressure of at least 30.6 inches over the Canadian Prairies on Sunday and Monday pushes ridging of at least 30.4 inches over the Upper Great Lakes on Sunday. The ridging intensifies to 30.6 inches Monday night into Tuesday morning as the high's center moves overhead. The high retreats east into New England by Wednesday morning.

30.4 inch high pressure is centered over Quebec this morning, with 29.4 inch low pressure positioned over northeastern Montana. Positioning of these surface features is resulting in generally south to southeasterly winds across the waters. Areas of fog, some of which has been dense, will continue through at least mid- morning, particularly over the western half of the waters. Dense Fog Advisory thus remains in effect until 10 AM CDT, with trends being monitored for possible extensions over the next hour. Aforementioned area of low pressure will progress toward Lake Winnipeg tonight, continuing on toward the Hudson Bay by Saturday evening as it deepens to near 29.2 inches. Progression of the low will maintain generally southerly flow across the waters, with gusts between 25-30 knots possible over the northern half of the lake Saturday afternoon and night. Can't rule out an isolated gust approaching gale force during this time frame, with conditions not expected to be widespread enough for headlines. Winds will trend southwesterly while steadily weakening ahead of an approaching cold front on Sunday. Currently expecting the front to move south across Lake Michigan late Sunday afterno
High pressure, 30.50 inches, over Quebec migrates south into New England to close out the week, sustaining an extended period of tranquil and mainly dry conditions into next week.

High pressure 30.50 inches over eastern Canada will continue to build south into the New England states and strengthen to 30.60 inches by Saturday. This high will continue south along the East Coast on Sunday. A weak front will cross the Great Lakes on Monday. High pressure 30.50 inches will return from the northeast on Tuesday.

A ridge averaging 30.5 inches affects the lake through Sunday night as the embedded high pressure center drifts generally southward from central Quebec toward the Mid-Atlantic states. The ridge then exits southeastward as a weak cold front sweeps southeastward across the lake on Monday. Behind the front, another ridge averaging 30.5 inches should build from central Canada and vicinity through this Tuesday.
